items.title: Every Mac comes with an (undocumented) family member classifier
items.summary: Apple's latest macOS includes an undocumented feature that classifies family members, potentially enhancing personalized user experiences. Developers should be aware of this capability for future app integrations and privacy considerations.

items.title: Libghostty 1.0 Released
items.summary: The release of Libghostty 1.0 introduces a new open-source library for terminal emulation, allowing developers to create more interactive command-line applications. This library simplifies the process of building terminal interfaces, making it a valuable tool for web and systems engineers.

items.title: A Jev that can ask Opus for help gives Opus accuracy at 4x lower cost
items.summary: A new AI model, Jev, can query another model, Opus, to enhance its accuracy while significantly reducing operational costs. This development highlights the potential for collaborative AI systems to optimize performance and resource utilization.

items.title: US FAA to phase out floppy disks from air traffic control by 2028
items.summary: The FAA's decision to phase out floppy disks marks a significant modernization step in air traffic control systems, emphasizing the need for updated technology in critical infrastructure. Engineers and developers in aviation tech should prepare for the transition to more secure and efficient data storage solutions.

items.title: Firecracker VM Escape: PwnEscape Part 2
items.summary: The second part of the PwnEscape series reveals vulnerabilities in Firecracker, a virtualization technology used by AWS, highlighting critical security implications for cloud-based applications. Developers should review their security practices in light of these findings to protect against potential exploits.
